analysis:
Examined the base text of DistributedInstalledPairServingGrant.swift (lines 1-786) together with the patch excerpt. The patch is truncated, so only part of the head is visible and no head-side line is available to cite.

Visible changes:
- ClusterPairServingGrant gains a `records` field. It holds the passing records that survive the same-shape divergence contradiction filter.
- A new `evidenceSHA256()` computes the SHA-256 of canonical JSON Lines of those records via ClusterConfigurationCodec.sha256.
- ClusterPairServingDecisions.init now passes `records:` into the grant at about head lines 475-476.
- The public-traffic-line and ownerServing/grant call sites at head lines 647-663 and 792-819 are touched. Their content is not visible, so those edits are unverified.

Security assessment: this is a provider-side derivation of an evidence digest. It adds no new network, key, or authorization surface. The grant stays chip-agnostic and is still gated by the coordinator's parity qualification, as the base comments say. `evidenceSHA256` is a pure hash over bundled records, so on the visible evidence there is no obvious weakening of the A-016/A-017 or TB-011 boundaries.

Remaining integration questions:
- Whether the digest, named as the grant's `evidence_sha256` in release cluster runtime facts, is verified by the coordinator or release publication. That code is outside the supplied evidence.
- The canonical JSON encoding in `encodedLine` (sorted keys, no whitespace) and whether a mismatch fails closed.
- What the patch changes in the head ranges 792-819 and 647-663, which are not visible. Public grant policy there should not have been loosened.

No concrete regression is supported by the supplied evidence. Because the patch excerpt is incomplete, deeper review is warranted.
